es: Reconocer recursos diplomáticos (I'm afraid, perhaps, slightly, I tend to) y ordenarlos según su grado de firmeza al discrepar.

teaching.en: I'm afraid I can't agree with the plan as it stands, but perhaps we could look at another option before we decide.
teaching.es: Me temo que no puedo estar de acuerdo con el plan tal como está, pero quizá podríamos mirar otra opción antes de decidir.

teaching.es: Con todo respeto, la fecha es algo temprana para la mayor parte del equipo, y el presupuesto parece bastante optimista.
teaching.explanationEs: with all due respect precede a una crítica firme; slightly y rather suavizan: «algo» y «bastante».
segments: With all due respect, the date is slightly too early for

teaching.en: Frankly, I tend to think that a shorter trip would be safer, although I may be wrong about the weather.
teaching.es: Sinceramente, tiendo a pensar que un viaje más corto sería más seguro, aunque puede que me equivoque con el clima.

teaching.en: A tactful colleague rarely says that you are wrong; she says instead that she sees the matter rather differently.
teaching.es: Un colega con tacto rara vez dice que te equivocas; dice, en cambio, que ve el asunto de forma bastante distinta.
teaching.explanationEs: tactful no significa ambiguo: se sigue diciendo lo que se piensa, pero sin atacar a la persona.
segments: A tactful colleague rarely says that you are wrong; she
says instead that she sees the matter rather differently.
teaching.audioText: A tactful colleague rarely says that you are wrong; she says instead that she sees the matter rather differently.

teaching.en: I wonder whether the date is fixed, because I suggest we ask everyone before we commit to anything.
teaching.es: Me pregunto si la fecha ya está fijada, porque sugiero que preguntemos a todos antes de comprometernos a nada.
teaching.explanationEs: I wonder whether + oración convierte un desacuerdo en una pregunta abierta; suggest, en una propuesta.
segments: I wonder whether the date is fixed, because I
suggest we ask everyone before we commit to anything.
teaching.audioText: I wonder whether the date is fixed, because I suggest we ask everyone before we commit to anything.

prompt.es: Elige la formulación más diplomática para rechazar la fecha propuesta.

choices.text: Monday at eight is impossible for me, so please choose another day.
I don't think Monday at eight works, so we have to change the date.
I'm afraid Monday at eight is slightly difficult for me; perhaps we could try later?

feedback.es: I'm afraid, slightly y perhaps suavizan el rechazo y ofrecen una salida; las otras dos son más directas y no proponen nada.

hint.es: Busca la que suma un suavizante y una propuesta en lugar de una orden.

origin.text: A colleague proposes holding the review meeting on Monday at eight. You cannot attend, but you want to keep the tone friendly and offer another option.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me temo que no puedo venir el viernes.»

feedback.es: I'm afraid abre un desacuerdo o un rechazo con tacto.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo con el que se abre una negativa amable.

origin.text: Thank you very much for the invitation. I'm ___ I cannot come on Friday, but I would love to meet you another day.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Quizá podríamos mirar otra opción antes de decidir.»

answer.text: Perhaps we could look at another option before we decide

feedback.es: Perhaps + could convierte la idea en una propuesta suave; before we decide marca el momento.

hint.es: Empieza con el adverbio que significa «quizá».

prompt.es: Une cada formulación con su grado de firmeza.

pairs: That idea will never work.
I disagree with that.
I'm afraid I see it slightly differently.
I wonder whether there might be another way to look at it.

feedback.es: La firmeza baja cuando se añaden I'm afraid o slightly, y más aún con una pregunta con I wonder whether.

pairs: That idea will never work.
I disagree with that.
I'm afraid I see it slightly differently.
I wonder whether there might be another way to look at it.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato de la reunión y elige qué propone Sara.

choices.text: Testing the idea on a smaller scale before committing.
Rejecting the proposal because the budget is too high.
Dropping the plan because Tom thinks it will not work.

feedback.es: Sara sugiere probar la idea a menor escala; dice que el presupuesto parece optimista, pero no rechaza la propuesta.

origin.audio: At the end of the meeting, the chair asked whether anyone wanted to add anything. Sara said that she appreciated the work behind the proposal, and that she was afraid she saw one difficulty. The budget seemed rather optimistic, and she wondered whether the team could test the idea on a smaller scale first. Then Tom, who tends to be blunt, said simply that the plan would not work. Nobody spoke for a moment, and the chair thanked Sara for her suggestion.

prompt.es: Completa cada frase con el recurso diplomático que encaja.

feedback.es: Suggest propone, rather suaviza el adjetivo tight y Perhaps + could introduce una alternativa.

sentences: I ___ we ask everyone before we commit to anything.

___ we could meet again on Thursday to discuss it?

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender Sara con su pregunta sobre el equipo?

choices.text: That she thinks the team has probably not had enough time.
That she has no opinion and only wants some information.
That she will accept the timetable once the figures are checked.
That she would prefer a different team to check the figures.

feedback.es: I wonder whether es una pregunta suavizada: Sara sugiere, sin afirmarlo, que el equipo no ha tenido tiempo suficiente.

origin.text: Dear Tom, thank you for your proposal. With all due respect, I'm not entirely convinced that the timetable is realistic, and I wonder whether the team has had enough time to check the figures. Perhaps we could discuss it on Thursday? Best wishes, Sara.

prompt.es: Completa cada espacio con el recurso que reconoce, suaviza o abre con franqueza.

feedback.es: Appreciate reconoce, tend to suaviza la opinión y Frankly abre con franqueza.

sentences: I ___ your offer, but I'm afraid the price is too high for us.
I ___ to think that a shorter trip would be safer for the group.
___, I think the plan needs more time before we approve it.
origin.text: Pistas en español: valorar, soler, sinceramente.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué grado de firmeza muestra Carlos.

choices.text: Warm: he fully supports the idea and only needs time to organise it.
Blunt: he rejects the idea openly, though without raising his voice.
Soft: he leaves room but shows a real doubt.

feedback.es: Elogia la idea pero añade que la fecha podría ser difícil y que necesita tiempo: suaviza el mensaje sin ocultar su duda.

origin.audio: Carlos answered the proposal after a long pause. He said that he appreciated the idea and that it was certainly interesting. Then he added that he would need some time to think, and that the date might be difficult. He did not say no, but he did not say yes either, and he avoided looking at Mia.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Con todo respeto, me temo que veo la situación de forma bastante distinta.»

answer.text: With all due respect I'm afraid I see the situation rather differently
accepted: With all due respect I'm afraid I see the situation rather differently
I'm afraid with all due respect I see the situation rather differently

feedback.es: With all due respect e I'm afraid se acumulan antes de la posición, y rather suaviza differently.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe Sara este mensaje a Tom?

choices.text: To reject the draft firmly and ask Tom to start again.
To thank Tom for the draft and tell him it needs no changes.
To ask for a change while keeping a friendly tone.
To warn Tom that the draft is late and must be finished at once.

feedback.es: Reconoce el trabajo y suaviza la crítica (slightly abrupt) para pedir un cambio y ofrecer su ayuda.

origin.text: Thank you for the draft, Tom. I appreciate how much work you put into it, and I'm afraid the ending seems slightly abrupt to me. Perhaps we could add a short paragraph? I would be glad to help with that.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me pregunto si podríamos hablar de otra fecha la semana próxima.»

answer.text: I wonder whether we could talk about another date next week

feedback.es: I wonder whether convierte un desacuerdo en una pregunta abierta sobre una alternativa.

prompt.es: Completa: «No estoy del todo convencido de que funcione tal como está.»

feedback.es: Not entirely convinced expresa duda sin rechazar el plan: un desacuerdo parcial y cortés.

origin.text: I would not call the plan a failure, but I am not ___ convinced that it will work in its present form.

es: Matizar un desacuerdo con distancia y concesión: seem y appear, might, somewhat, arguably, preguntas indirectas con whether y los conectores albeit y notwithstanding.

teaching.en: The plan seems somewhat expensive for a small club, although it would seem that the members are willing to pay more.
teaching.es: El plan parece algo caro para un club pequeño, aunque parecería que los socios están dispuestos a pagar más.
teaching.explanationEs: seem + adjetivo presenta una impresión; somewhat baja la fuerza; it would seem that toma aún más distancia.
segments: The plan seems somewhat expensive for a small club, although it
would seem that the members are willing to pay more.
teaching.audioText: The plan seems somewhat expensive for a small club, although it would seem that the members are willing to pay more.

teaching.en: Some members appear to have a different view, and the committee might possibly need more time than it has.
teaching.es: Algunos socios parecen tener una opinión distinta, y el comité quizá necesite más tiempo del que tiene.
teaching.explanationEs: appear to + verbo describe cómo parece algo; might + possibly acumula dos suavizantes de posibilidad.
segments: Some members appear to have a different view, and the
committee might possibly need more time than it has.
teaching.audioText: Some members appear to have a different view, and the committee might possibly need more time than it has.

teaching.en: That is arguably the safest option, albeit not the cheapest, and to a certain extent it reflects what members asked for.
teaching.es: Esa es posiblemente la opción más segura, aunque no la más barata, y hasta cierto punto refleja lo que pidieron los socios.
teaching.explanationEs: albeit + grupo breve: concesión corta; to a certain extent limita el alcance de lo que afirmas.
segments: That is arguably the safest option, albeit not the cheapest, and
to a certain extent it reflects what members asked for.
teaching.audioText: That is arguably the safest option, albeit not the cheapest, and to a certain extent it reflects what members asked for.

teaching.en: Notwithstanding the cost, I think the trip is worth it, although it could be argued that a cheaper venue would do just as well.
teaching.es: A pesar del costo, creo que el viaje vale la pena, aunque se podría argumentar que un lugar más barato serviría igual de bien.
teaching.explanationEs: notwithstanding + nombre reconoce un punto contrario; it could be argued that presenta una objeción sin hacerla tuya.
segments: Notwithstanding the cost, I think the trip is worth it, although it
could be argued that a cheaper venue would do just as well.
teaching.audioText: Notwithstanding the cost, I think the trip is worth it, although it could be argued that a cheaper venue would do just as well.

teaching.en: Could you tell me whether the budget is already fixed, or whether the committee is still looking at other options?
teaching.es: ¿Podrías decirme si el presupuesto ya está fijado, o si el comité todavía está estudiando otras opciones?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta indirecta: whether + orden de afirmación, sin inversión del auxiliar.
segments: Could you tell me whether the budget is already fixed,
or whether the committee is still looking at other options?
teaching.audioText: Could you tell me whether the budget is already fixed, or whether the committee is still looking at other options?

teaching.en: Hedging does not mean avoiding the point: a careful verb and an adverb such as somewhat let you say what you think without closing the conversation.
teaching.es: Matizar no es esquivar el asunto: un verbo prudente y un adverbio como «algo» permiten decir lo que piensas sin cerrar la conversación.
teaching.explanationEs: El objetivo de matizar es que la otra persona pueda seguir hablando contigo, no borrar tu opinión.
segments: Hedging does not mean avoiding the point: a careful verb and an adverb
such as somewhat let you say what you think without closing the conversation.
teaching.audioText: Hedging does not mean avoiding the point: a careful verb and an adverb such as somewhat let you say what you think without closing the conversation.

prompt.es: Elige la versión con seem que suaviza la frase directa sobre el presupuesto.

choices.text: Your plan seems somewhat expensive compared with our budget.
Your plan is seeming somewhat expensive compared with our budget.
Your plan seems that it is somewhat expensive for our budget.

feedback.es: Seem + adjetivo funciona sin más (seems somewhat expensive); seem no se usa en forma continua ni con that + it is después de seems.

hint.es: Busca la opción en la que seem va directamente con el adjetivo.

origin.text: A colleague's plan for the club dinner will cost twice the agreed budget. You want to say so without sounding hostile.

feedback.es: Whether introduce una pregunta indirecta con orden de afirmación.

feedback.es: Appear to + verbo presenta la opinión como una impresión; rather suaviza different.

choices.text: It is ambitious, so she wants the club to choose a smaller event.
It is promising, but she has doubts about time and support.
It is the club's best idea in years, and she has no doubts about it.

feedback.es: Matiza con seemed somewhat ambitious, might possibly y una pregunta sobre los patrocinadores: valora la idea pero deja ver dudas.

origin.audio: At the club meeting, the treasurer summarised the proposal for the tournament. The plan, she said, seemed somewhat ambitious, albeit well organised, and it might possibly need more time than the committee had. Notwithstanding the cost, she thought the idea was arguably the club's best in years. She asked whether the sponsors had confirmed their support, and several members appeared to share her doubts. The chair said that he would ask them again on Monday.

choices.text: Could you tell me whether has the room a projector?
Could you tell me does the room have a projector?
Could you tell me whether the room has a projector?

feedback.es: En la pregunta indirecta se usa whether + orden de afirmación: whether the room has a projector.

origin.text: Dear Sir or Madam, we are booking a room for our yearly meeting next month. Before we confirm the booking, we would like to ask you a question about the equipment, because some of our members will give presentations during the morning session.

feedback.es: Albeit introduce una concesión breve sin verbo conjugado.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué actitud muestran los autores ante sus datos.

choices.text: Cautious: they present the link as possible, not proven.
Optimistic: they see the link as real and expect larger samples to confirm it.
Dismissive: they treat the link as too weak to be worth mentioning.

feedback.es: Seem to, weak, might possibly y stop short of una conclusión firme muestran cautela: el vínculo es posible, no demostrado.

origin.audio: The report says that the data seem to point to a link between sleep and memory, albeit a weak one. The authors add that the effect might possibly disappear in larger samples. They stop short of any firm conclusion, and arguably that caution is the most honest part of the whole article.

prompt.es: ¿Qué busca Sara con este mensaje al grupo?

choices.text: To ask the group to cancel the party because the room is too small.
To blame whoever sent out so many invitations.
To insist that the hotel must give a larger room.
To raise a doubt without blaming anyone and ask for help.

feedback.es: Con it would appear, may, might y perhaps plantea un problema posible, no un reproche, y pide que alguien lo compruebe.

origin.text: Dear all, it would appear that the room may be somewhat small for the party, since more guests have replied than we expected. I might be wrong, and perhaps the hotel can offer a larger one. Could someone find out whether that is possible? Thanks, Sara.

prompt.es: Suaviza la frase directa con seem o appear y un modal de posibilidad.

answer.text: The schedule seems somewhat tight, and the team might not finish on time.
accepted: The schedule seems somewhat tight, and the team might not finish on time.
The schedule appears to be rather tight, and the team might not be able to finish on time.
It seems that the schedule is somewhat tight, and that the team might not finish on time.

feedback.es: Seem o appear convierten «is too tight» en una impresión, y might suaviza la predicción.

origin.text: Frase directa: «The schedule is too tight and the team will not finish on time.» Reescríbela con seem o appear y might.

feedback.es: Arguably marca que es una opinión defendible, no un hecho.

origin.text: Several options were considered during the meeting. This is ___ the best one, although the others have some merits as well.

es: Interpretar rechazos y dudas corteses en diálogos orales (That might be difficult, I'll think about it) y decidir si la persona acepta, duda o rechaza, citando la frase que lo indica.

teaching.en: When Sara says “That might be difficult”, she is trying to decline without causing offence, and most listeners will hear a polite no.
teaching.es: Cuando Sara dice «Eso podría ser difícil», intenta rechazar sin ofender, y la mayoría de los oyentes entenderá un no cortés.
teaching.explanationEs: «That might be difficult» casi siempre es un no educado: el modal might suaviza la negativa.
segments: When Sara says “That might be difficult”, she is trying to decline
without causing offence, and most listeners will hear a polite no.
teaching.audioText: When Sara says “That might be difficult”, she is trying to decline without causing offence, and most listeners will hear a polite no.

teaching.en: “I'll think about it” often shows that the speaker is hesitant, and without a date or a reason it is usually a lukewarm response.
teaching.es: «Lo pensaré» suele mostrar que quien habla está indeciso, y sin fecha ni motivo suele ser una respuesta tibia.
teaching.explanationEs: hesitant: no ha dicho que sí; a lukewarm response carece de entusiasmo y de compromiso concreto.
segments: “I'll think about it” often shows that the speaker is hesitant, and
without a date or a reason it is usually a lukewarm response.
teaching.audioText: “I'll think about it” often shows that the speaker is hesitant, and without a date or a reason it is usually a lukewarm response.

teaching.en: Carlos sounded reluctant to commit to the trip, even though his words were friendly and he promised to call on Friday.
teaching.es: Carlos sonó reacio a comprometerse con el viaje, aunque sus palabras eran amables y prometió llamar el viernes.
teaching.explanationEs: reluctant: no quiere hacerlo pero no lo dice con palabras; commit to + nombre o -ing.
segments: Carlos sounded reluctant to commit to the trip, even though his
words were friendly and he promised to call on Friday.
teaching.audioText: Carlos sounded reluctant to commit to the trip, even though his words were friendly and he promised to call on Friday.

teaching.en: Listen to the tone: a flat voice can turn a friendly sentence into a polite no, and a long pause can say even more.
teaching.es: Escucha el tono: una voz plana puede convertir una frase amable en un no cortés, y una pausa larga puede decir aún más.
teaching.explanationEs: El tono y las pausas cambian el significado de una frase, aunque las palabras sean amables.
segments: Listen to the tone: a flat voice can turn a friendly sentence
into a polite no, and a long pause can say even more.
teaching.audioText: Listen to the tone: a flat voice can turn a friendly sentence into a polite no, and a long pause can say even more.

teaching.en: Ana took the hint and stopped asking, because Tom had tried twice to stall for time instead of answering.
teaching.es: Ana captó la indirecta y dejó de preguntar, porque Tom había intentado dos veces ganar tiempo en lugar de responder.
teaching.explanationEs: take the hint: entender lo que alguien insinúa sin decirlo; stall for time: dar largas.
segments: Ana took the hint and stopped asking, because Tom had
tried twice to stall for time instead of answering.
teaching.audioText: Ana took the hint and stopped asking, because Tom had tried twice to stall for time instead of answering.

teaching.en: A flat refusal is rare in polite conversation, so listeners must interpret what is left unsaid and weigh the evidence in the words.
teaching.es: Una negativa rotunda es rara en una conversación cortés, así que quien escucha debe interpretar lo que queda sin decir y sopesar las pistas de las palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: interpret: leer entre líneas; la decisión (acepta, duda, rechaza) se apoya en la frase exacta que la indica.
segments: A flat refusal is rare in polite conversation, so listeners must interpret
what is left unsaid and weigh the evidence in the words.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la respuesta «Maybe another time» en este intercambio?

choices.text: She is accepting, but wants to arrive a little late.
She is politely declining and leaving the door open.
She is hesitant and needs a few days to decide.

feedback.es: Sin motivo, fecha ni alternativa, «maybe another time» es un rechazo cortés; no da tiempo para decidir.

hint.es: Fíjate en si la respuesta da un día concreto o pide tiempo.

origin.text: Invitation: “We're all going climbing on Friday. Do you want to join us?” Answer: “That sounds lovely. Maybe another time.” The speaker gives no reason and suggests no date.

feedback.es: Take the hint significa entender lo que alguien insinúa sin decirlo.

choices.text: He accepts, but needs a little more time to confirm.
He is hesitant and wants to hear more details.
He declines politely, without suggesting another day.

feedback.es: El «but» (though) después del elogio, la agenda ocupada y la falta de alternativa indican un rechazo cortés.

hint.es: Busca el contraste después del elogio y si hay alguna alternativa.

Leo, who says the week is full.
Tom, who says he is very sorry.

origin.audio: Five friends were invited to the opening of a new café. Mia replied at once that she would be there at six and would bring the cake. Leo said it sounded lovely but that his week was very full, and that they should meet some other time. Ana answered that she would think about it and let them know. Tom wrote that he was very sorry, but he had to work. Carlos said he would love to come and asked whether he could bring a friend.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje y elige cómo interpretar la respuesta de la persona.

choices.text: She accepts, but wants to choose the hour herself.
She is hesitant: she has not decided and will reply later.
She declines flatly and closes the subject for good.

feedback.es: «I'll think about it» y «let me see» muestran duda: no hay respuesta todavía, ni un sí ni un no rotundo.

origin.audio: Hmm, I'll think about it. Let me see how my week goes, and I'll let you know. It's just that I have so much on at the moment, and I hate to promise something I might not be able to do.

prompt.es: Une cada frase cortés con su lectura real.

I'd be glad to help, though I can only stay an hour.

feedback.es: Un compromiso concreto es aceptar, «let me see» es dudar, un modal suavizado rechaza y un límite de tiempo es una condición.

pairs: Count me in; I'll bring the cake.
Let me see how my week goes.
That might be difficult, I'm afraid.
I'd be glad to help, though I can only stay an hour.

choices.text: She will come if Mia moves the dinner to Sunday.
She has another plan for Saturday and feels annoyed.

prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje de reparación de Mia a Tom (unas 170 palabras).

answer.text: Dear Tom, I think there was a misunderstanding at the dinner on Friday, and I would like to clear the air. I did not intend to offend you, and I am very sorry that my insistence on paying may have come across as rude. In my country it is a custom for the person who invites to pay for everybody, and refusing your offer was my way of showing respect, not of ignoring you. I can see now that it may have given the wrong impression, since in Scotland friends usually share the bill. I apologise for not explaining this at the time, and I hope you will give me the benefit of the doubt. Let me clarify something else: I enjoyed the evening very much, and I appreciate your honesty when you told me how you felt. Perhaps we could meet halfway next time: I will choose the restaurant, and you will pay for the dessert. Would you like to have lunch on Saturday? I promise to ask before I reach for the bill. Kind regards, Mia

Hello Tom, I am sorry about the confusion at the dinner. I think we had a misunderstanding, and I never meant to hurt you. Where I come from, the person who invites usually pays for everybody, so when I refused your offer I wanted to show respect, but I see that it may have given the wrong impression and come across as rude to you. I apologise for not explaining that at the moment. Let me clarify: I had a lovely evening, and I want to keep our friendship. I appreciate that you told me how you felt, and I hope you can give me the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps we could go out again on Saturday, and this time we could split the bill so that nobody feels uncomfortable. Would you like that? Thank you for listening.
